      "title": "Cancelled reminders are deleted before SendGrid cancellation",
      "body": "The first `deleteMany` removes all EMAIL reminders with `scheduledDate <= now`, including those marked `cancelled: true`. The subsequent cancellation query (lines 43-51) looks for reminders with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. If a cancelled reminder's scheduledDate has already passed (e.g., it was cancelled just before its send time), it is deleted from the database by the first `deleteMany`, so the SendGrid cancellation request is never sent, and the email is still delivered. This defeats the purpose of the PR for reminders that are cancelled after their scheduled time but before SendGrid actually sends. The first `deleteMany` should exclude `cancelled: true`, or the cancellation step should run before any deletion."

    {
      "file": "packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts",

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "immediateDelete sends cancellation but leaves stale DB row",
      "body": "When `immediateDelete` is true, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` sends the SendGrid cancellation and then `return`s without deleting the `workflowReminder` row or setting the `cancelled` flag. This leaves a row with `scheduled: true` and `referenceId` still pointing to a cancelled batch. In rescheduling (handleNewBooking.ts), this row persists associated with the cancelled booking, potentially for days until its `scheduledDate` passes. It may also be processed again later by `handleCancelBooking` if the same booking is cancelled again, causing duplicate cancellation attempts. The function should either delete the DB row or set `cancelled: true` after successful SendGrid cancellation."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts",
      "line": 485,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Async reminder cancellation calls are not awaited",
      "body": "Within the `forEach` over `updatedBookings`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called but their promises are not awaited or collected. These functions perform external API calls (SendGrid, Twilio) and DB updates. The handler proceeds to `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` and then returns, so the API may signal successful cancellation before the reminder cancellations have actually completed. If the process crashes or the client assumes cancellation is fully done, reminders may still be sent. The async calls should be collected and awaited (e.g., using `Promise.all`)."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts",
      "line": 966,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Async reminder cancellation in reschedule is not awaited",
      "body": "In the reschedule path, the loop over `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without awaiting them (the `forEach` callback is not async and no promises are collected). This means the new booking's workflow reminders may be scheduled before the old reminders have been fully cancelled at SendGrid/Twilio, and the function could return before cancellation completes. The calls should be awaited or their promises aggregated."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts",
      "line": 56,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Cancellation loop aborts on first SendGrid error",
      "body": "The entire cancellation process is wrapped in a single try/catch. Inside the `for` loop, if `client.request` throws for one reminder, the catch block logs the error and exits, skipping all remaining reminders and also preventing the queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` operations from running (since the promises are not awaited before the exception). This can leave many cancelled reminders uncancelled at SendGrid and in the database. Errors should be handled per reminder, or the loop should continue after logging."
    }

findings.title: Cancelled reminders are deleted before SendGrid cancellation
findings.body: The first `deleteMany` removes all EMAIL reminders with `scheduledDate <= now`, including those marked `cancelled: true`. The subsequent cancellation query (lines 43-51) looks for reminders with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. If a cancelled reminder's scheduledDate has already passed (e.g., it was cancelled just before its send time), it is deleted from the database by the first `deleteMany`, so the SendGrid cancellation request is never sent, and the email is still delivered. This defeats the purpose of the PR for reminders that are cancelled after their scheduled time but before SendGrid actually sends. The first `deleteMany` should exclude `cancelled: true`, or the cancellation step should run before any deletion.

findings.title: immediateDelete sends cancellation but leaves stale DB row
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` sends the SendGrid cancellation and then `return`s without deleting the `workflowReminder` row or setting the `cancelled` flag. This leaves a row with `scheduled: true` and `referenceId` still pointing to a cancelled batch. In rescheduling (handleNewBooking.ts), this row persists associated with the cancelled booking, potentially for days until its `scheduledDate` passes. It may also be processed again later by `handleCancelBooking` if the same booking is cancelled again, causing duplicate cancellation attempts. The function should either delete the DB row or set `cancelled: true` after successful SendGrid cancellation.

findings.title: Async reminder cancellation calls are not awaited
findings.body: Within the `forEach` over `updatedBookings`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called but their promises are not awaited or collected. These functions perform external API calls (SendGrid, Twilio) and DB updates. The handler proceeds to `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` and then returns, so the API may signal successful cancellation before the reminder cancellations have actually completed. If the process crashes or the client assumes cancellation is fully done, reminders may still be sent. The async calls should be collected and awaited (e.g., using `Promise.all`).

findings.title: Async reminder cancellation in reschedule is not awaited
findings.body: In the reschedule path, the loop over `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without awaiting them (the `forEach` callback is not async and no promises are collected). This means the new booking's workflow reminders may be scheduled before the old reminders have been fully cancelled at SendGrid/Twilio, and the function could return before cancellation completes. The calls should be awaited or their promises aggregated.

findings.title: Cancellation loop aborts on first SendGrid error
findings.body: The entire cancellation process is wrapped in a single try/catch. Inside the `for` loop, if `client.request` throws for one reminder, the catch block logs the error and exits, skipping all remaining reminders and also preventing the queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` operations from running (since the promises are not awaited before the exception). This can leave many cancelled reminders uncancelled at SendGrid and in the database. Errors should be handled per reminder, or the loop should continue after logging.
